_note: Modes to cover, per category. The point of this file is that the mode list
comes from OUTSIDE one person's imagination: #492 measured that covering
missing modes is what improves detection, and that the scam corpus was
missing authority-threat and verify-at-a-link precisely because the list
was invented unaided.
coercive-control and harassment-bullying carry the most modes on purpose —
they are the two categories the system handles worst, and the two with no
public conversational corpus anywhere. Their modes are taken from the NSW
BOCSAR / Crime Science text-mining study of 406,196 police narratives
(Kim & Karystianis 2024), which is a frequency-ordered account of what
these behaviours actually look like rather than what we imagine.
It is a COMPLEMENT, not a definition: police narratives record observable
acts, so gaslighting and the silent treatment do not appear in the study
and are added here from our own fixtures.

_note: The hard part, and where every false alarm this project has measured
lives. Each of these deliberately shares surface features with a harmful
mode above — the words look similar, the intent is not. A corpus of only
positives teaches a model to flag ordinary care.
